text:
jamie: quick brain dump 1: we keep hitting complexity in lease-transfer. alternative: introduce a "graceful-degrade" flow that buffers a small tail window (e.g., 4s / 256 tokens) and if upstream fails within that window, we either: 1) replay from cache, 2) rerun non-stream with idempotency, or 3) emit a short degraded trailer and close. cheaper than full resumable protocol and better UX than immediate hard abort.

rahul: curious about memory / concurrency costs. buffering per-conn tail for many concurrent streams could blow up. can we bound it? e.g., max_buffer_per_route and a global max_buffer_pool. if pool exhausted -> fast-fail to fallback.

jamie: exactly, config knobs per-route: {"tail_window_ms":4000, "max_buffer_bytes":262144, "fallback_order": ["cache","rerun","trailer"]}. also backpressure: if buffer fills, start shedding oldest partial tokens for that connection and mark as truncated.

toni: semantics for side-effects? if model invoked tools before failure, rerun is risky. we should prefer cache when available and require idempotency for rerun. if no idempotency and no cache -> emit 409-ish degraded error payload.

kai: implementation sketch: on upstream midstream-error -> mark connection in DEGRADING state, keep buffer for tail_window_ms, send SSE event {"edge:degrading": true}, attempt cache lookup concurrently, if cached -> flush single payload, else if idempotency -> issue non-stream retry, else after tail window -> send trailer {"degraded":true, "reason":"no_idempotency"} and close.

jamie: pseudocode:
```
if midstream_error:
  set_state(conn, 'DEGRADING')
  emit_sse(conn, {degrading:true})
  concurrent: cache_lookup = cache.get(req.key)
  wait up to tail_window_ms for cache_lookup or rerun
  if cache_lookup.hit: send_single_chunk(cache.lookup)
  elif req.has_idempotency: resp = backend.call_nonstream(req); send_single_chunk(resp)
  else: send_trailer(conn, {degraded:true})
```

rahul: observability: metric edge.degrade.tail_buffered_count, edge.degrade.truncated_count, edge.degrade.cache_hit, edge.degrade.rerun_count. trace span should include degrade_phase and buffer_usage_bytes. also important: billing tag degrade_path=true to avoid double-charge.

toni: tests: unit for state transitions, integration: simulate midstream error and assert buffer behavior, load test: ensure global buffer pool prevents OOM. infra-bot: add feature flag ingress.graceful_degrade and schema changes.

infra-bot: checklist created: update config schema, add feature flag ingress.graceful_degrade, implement buffer pool, add metrics & traces, add integration and stress tests.

kai: UX: SDK should show small banner on `edge:degrading` SSE and handle single chunk arrival. also allow client to opt-out of buffering via header X-Edge-Prefer-No-Buffer: true (for ultra-low-latency apps).

jamie: rollout plan: behind flag -> internal canary (non-critical routes) 72h -> enable for free/standard -> keep enterprise on resume until we vet. I'll write short RFC addendum with diagrams contrasting lease-transfer vs tail-buffer degrade.

rahul: +1. please include worst-case memory calc per-region in RFC so oncall knows limits.

jamie: will do. thanks team.
